title: Customer-Centric Model Impact Storyboard: Scenario Tests for SLA-aligned Fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a concise, executable storyboard that ties customer SLA profiles to concrete model-swap scenarios, cost/latency breakpoints, and procurement triggers. The artifact will guide engineering + sales when a model becomes degraded, unavailable, or economically suboptimal for a given enterprise RAG workload.

Scope: 1) Identify 6 canonical enterprise RAG customer archetypes (e.g., high-availability finserv, cost-sensitive marketplace search, low-latency internal assistant). 2) For each archetype, define 3 failure/pressure modes (regional outage, model quality regression, sudden price spike). 3) For each mode produce a stepwise failover plan: preferred fallbacks, estimated token-cost delta, latency delta, user-visible impact, and procurement/contract actions. 4) Produce a runbook with thresholds (latency percentiles, error rates, token price change) that trigger routing or procurement escalation.

Why now: Sales and SRE teams are repeatedly requesting prescriptive, customer-facing playbooks for model outages and price shocks. Current materials are high-level; customers want concrete numbers and scripted decision flows they can operate from. This ticket produces a living storyboard to be referenced in enterprise onboarding and runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Six customer archetypes documented with one representative synthetic workload and expected token/embedding usage profile
Three pressure modes per archetype with quantifiable metrics (latency p95, error rate, token price change) that define thresholds
Fallback matrix: for each pressure mode, at least two vetted fallback model variants with estimated token-cost and latency deltas
Playbook pages: one per archetype that includes escalation steps, customer messaging templates, and procurement trigger checklists
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Solutions, SRE, and Legal (security/compliance implications documented)
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: met with SRE (Lena Park) and Solutions (Marco Ruiz). Agreed to prioritize finserv and marketplace archetypes first. Noted need for embargoed cost estimates for sales demos.

2026-03-02 - Data pull: engineering provided p95 latency baselines and token counters for representative workloads (see links). Observed KV cache hit-rate variance drives 30-40% token cost swing for retrieval-heavy RAG.

2026-03-05 - Drafted initial fallback matrix. Engineering flagged two risky assumptions: 1) quantized model latency parity in short context; 2) cross-region cold-starts adding 70-120ms. Added follow-up tasks to validate with bench lab.

2026-03-08 - Review with Solutions and Sales: Sales requested explicit customer messaging for 'We may switch models temporarily to preserve SLA' and a canned SLO-affecting incident script. Added messaging templates to playbook.
2026-03-10 - Legal/Compliance pass: privacy team required an appendix documenting data residency and KMS implications for model fallbacks that cross regions. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12 - Engineering lab results: validated fallback candidates for finserv archetype; cost delta estimates refined. Ready for stakeholder sign-off pending SRE review of automated routing thresholds.
